failures.criterion: A3/A4 on the surface a person reaches: the room budget and the apply, copy and refusal bounds hold the pod Dispatch actually runs in
failures.evidence: Every bound this change adds is a compile-time constant derived from a 4 GiB container, while the runtime's own limit follows the container: setGoMemoryLimit reads the cgroup at boot (cmd/dispatch/main.go:165-193). The constants: goMemoryLimitBytes = 4 << 30 * 9 / 10 (peer_update.go:1539, its comment calls it 'the Go runtime's soft memory limit on the production pod'); roomBudgetBytes = 2 << 30 (room_budget.go:41); heapAboveTheReserve = 1,181,116,006 (peer_update.go:1550); applyHeapBound = 393,705,335 (peer_update.go:1581); copyHeapBound (copy_heap.go:59); applyTooHeavyBytes = heapAboveTheReserve (peer_update.go:1633). Production is not a 4 GiB pod: theorem-labs/agent-infra dispatch/Pulumi.prod.yaml on main reads agent-infra-dispatch:appCpu: "16" and agent-infra-dispatch:appMemory: 32Gi, and its own comment records the INFRA lead raising the envoy-dispatch container by hand on 2026-10-26 (dispatch://INFRA-394) to 16 CPU and, at 23:33:55Z, 32Gi, with the keys declared 'so an apply keeps it rather than reverting to 1 CPU and 4Gi'. That raise is one day before this issue was admitted (2026-10-27T13:48:41Z). Spec v23's premise, 'one pod with a 4 GiB memory limit', cites infra/gcp/dispatch_kube.go:459, which is the gcp:Dispatch component's default, not the deployment. I searched cmd/dispatch/settings.go: no setting overrides the room budget or any derived bound; GOMEMLIMIT and AUTOMEMLIMIT move the runtime limit and move none of them. What that does on the pod that runs: open rooms are capped at 2 GiB of 32 GiB (6 per cent), so the 38th one-mebibyte document is closed 4503 DOC_BUSY and resident rooms are closed with about 29 GiB free; applyTooHeavyBytes refuses an edit 4413 DOC_TOO_LARGE with 'the update is heavier to apply than the pod can hold' past 1.18 GB against a real limit near 30.9 GB, a sentence that is false there, with only 23 per cent of margin left for honest traffic (the heaviest honest handoff is estimated at 904,378,600 against the 1,181,116,006 line, peer_update.go:1627-1629); and the 375 MiB apply and copy bounds serialise work a 32 GiB pod could run together, measured in the change's own drives on this pod as copy-bound waits of 27.253 s (burst) and 21.014 s (heaviest apply). The safety goal still holds: bounds sized for 4 GiB are stricter than a 32 GiB pod needs, so nothing here can kill the pod, and today's corpus (spec v23's census: 825 live documents, 13.63 MiB of text, largest 1,021.6 KiB, about 0.7 GiB with every one open) does not reach the 2 GiB budget. The architect decided on 2026-11-01T11:04:02Z that this is a defect in this change's own code, fixed in this pull request and needing no new spec version: the room budget, the reserve, the apply and copy bounds and applyTooHeavyBytes are to be derived from the Go limit the runtime holds after boot, equal to today's constants at a 3.6 GiB limit and scaled above it, with the 4 GiB calibration as the fallback when no limit is readable, and the boot line naming each derived bound beside the limit.
failures.redTest: none written: the remedy is a design change the architect specified, and a red test pinning today's constants would have to be deleted by the fix it pins. The evidence above is the pin.

failures.criterion: A person typing in an ordinary room is answered while the server does its heavy work (the change's own assertion, browser_memory_test.go:2894: p99 under 2 s and none over 5 s)
failures.evidence: TestTheHeaviestApplyBesideAFullCopyBoundStaysUnderThePodsMemory is red one run in three on this pod, on that assertion alone and never on a memory figure. Command, each run alone on an idle pod (load average 0.00), nothing else running: cd packages/envoy && DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=$LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN go test -tags memory -p 1 -count=1 -run '^TestTheHeaviestApplyBesideAFullCopyBoundStaysUnderThePodsMemory$' -v -timeout 60m ./cmd/dispatch/. Run 1 (09:21:34Z-09:28:35Z) FAIL: 'keystrokes in an ordinary room during the cache's fill were answered in p99 2.816s and at most 3.204s, want p99 under 2 s and none over 5 s: typing waited behind the heavy work' (147 keystrokes, p50 2ms, p90 20ms). Run 2 (09:29:10Z-09:36:26Z) PASS: 169 keystrokes, p50 3ms, p90 25ms, p99 100ms, max 282ms. Run 3 (11:02:56Z-11:10:04Z) PASS: 163 keystrokes, p50 1ms, p90 14ms, p99 100ms, max 3.379s. So the multi-second stall is in two runs of the three (max 3.204 s and 3.379 s) and only run 1 caught enough keystrokes in it to move p99 past 2 s; it is a real stall a person would see, not only a test that is tight. Every memory assertion passed in all three (the heaviest step held +59,442, +20,752,482 and +4,085,810 bytes over the 3,865,470,566-byte Go limit, each inside the 128 MiB margin; charged peaks 3,207, 3,271 and 3,241 MiB of 4,096). The six dispatch-memory shards of CI run 41287414180 passed at cef56589, so CI is not showing it yet; a test red one run in three will block later merges whoever makes them. The architect's instruction (2026-11-01T11:04:02Z): find the cause (a keystroke waiting behind a bound, the collector, or the test pod's load) and fix it in the product if a person would see it, never by loosening the assertion. Note for that search: production Dispatch runs 16 CPU (dispatch/Pulumi.prod.yaml) and this pod has 2, so CPU starvation here is not production's shape, but the stall sits in the same window as the copy bound's 21.014 s longest wait.

One silent socket asked for the room's whole state 512 times and was closed on the direct send path with 63,117,516 bytes queued and a 3,005,596-byte frame refused, against its 62,914,560-byte budget; the 512-frame cap alone would have let it hold 1,538,884,096. Twenty such sockets held 1,258,425,600 bytes between them when they were closed, where the frame cap alone would have allowed 10,738,944,000; charged 2,082 MiB of 4,096. The honest reader is the refused-party control in reverse: the same budget, the same burst, never closed.
